limits: Metrics tables (9-1, 9-2) are stated to be illustrative, not benchmarks.
Fused L2-norm example miscounts kernels (4 vs three) and byte totals.
Text names Blackwell-specific features (TMEM, tcgen05) as written for 2025 hardware; vendor peak figures are uncited.
Unified-memory and prefetch advice is hardware-generation specific; SASS is not forward compatible.
practices: Raise FLOPs per byte with tiling, on-chip reuse, fusion and larger batches; verify on the Nsight Compute roofline (Intro).
Use multilevel tiling: shared-memory tile, then register micro-tiles with float4/half2; coalesce loads and pad/swizzle (Multilevel Microtiling).
Double-buffer with asynchronous loads (cuda::memcpy_async, TMA) to overlap transfers with compute (Software Prefetching, Feeding Tensor Cores).
Profile fused kernels: too much fusion raises register pressure, lowers occupancy and may spill (Kernel Fusion).
Apply tiling, coalescing and fusion before 2:4 structured sparsity; use sparsity for inference only, and fine-tune after pruning (Structured Sparsity).
Recompute cheap values instead of loading them when bandwidth is the bottleneck (Recomputation).
Prefer fused PyTorch ops, torch.compile and nested tensors; verify backend selection for SDPA (PyTorch and Arithmetic Intensity).
Prefer BF16 over FP16 for training; use FP8/NVFP4 only after calibration and per-model accuracy validation (BF16/FP16, FP8, FP4).
Keep batch or tile size large enough that FP8/FP4/sparse paths amortize overhead (Mixed Precision).
Use CUTLASS and libraries built on it for standard GEMM and fused attention; hand-write MMA only for unusual layouts or fusions (Using CUTLASS).
Use inline PTX/SASS last, isolated, documented and re-profiled per GPU generation (Inline PTX and SASS Tuning).
